Steps: 1) Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out if comfortable. 2) Brace your trunk, bend your knees, and sit your hips back and down. 3) Lower to a comfortable depth while keeping your heels grounded. 4) Press through your whole foot to stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top. 5) As you rise, gently reach one arm back and open your chest, then alternate sides.
Best Practices: 1) Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes. 2) Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches. 3) Choose a range where you can keep control and balance. 4) Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Steps: 1) Stand tall with feet under hips and brace your trunk. 2) Step into the lunge with one foot and lower until both knees bend comfortably. 3) Keep the front knee tracking over the middle toes and your torso controlled. 4) Push through the front foot to return to standing. 5) After standing, lift the back leg behind you by squeezing the glute, then reset.
Best Practices: 1) Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes. 2) Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches. 3) Choose a range where you can keep control and balance. 4) Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Name: Stair Climber Step-Up
Short Description: Alternate brisk step-ups on a stair while keeping posture tall.
Steps: 1) Stand facing a low, stable step or stair. 2) Place one foot fully on the step with the knee tracking over the toes. 3) Press through the stepping foot to stand tall on the step. 4) Step back down with control and repeat, switching sides as planned.
Best Practices: 1) Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes. 2) Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches. 3) Choose a range where you can keep control and balance. 4) Use only a stable surface that will not slide, tip, or open unexpectedly. 5) Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Steps: 1) Set up under a sturdy table or at a secure door frame only if it can safely support you. 2) Hold the edge or frame and keep your body in a straight line. 3) Pull your chest toward your hands by driving elbows back. 4) Lower under control and repeat.
Best Practices: 1) Start each pull by setting shoulder blades gently back and down. 2) Avoid shrugging or craning your neck. 3) Move slowly enough to feel the upper back, not momentum. 4) Use only a stable surface that will not slide, tip, or open unexpectedly. 5) Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Steps: 1) Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart and a little space around you. 2) Move slowly into the stretch or mobility position until you feel mild tension, not pain. 3) Trace wide figure-eights with the arms to mobilize shoulders and upper back. 4) Breathe steadily, then ease out and switch sides if the movement is one-sided.
Best Practices: 1) Move slowly enough that breathing stays calm. 2) Treat flows as coordination practice, not a race. 3) Use props or smaller ranges to make the sequence feel restorative. 4) A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.

Name: Seated Full-Body Side Stretch
Short Description: Sit tall, hold the chair lightly, and reach one arm overhead into a gentle side stretch.
Steps: 1) Sit tall on a chair with both feet grounded. 2) Reach one arm overhead and place the other hand on the chair or thigh. 3) Lean gently to the side until you feel the side body stretch. 4) Return to center and switch sides.
Best Practices: 1) Move slowly enough that breathing stays calm. 2) Treat flows as coordination practice, not a race. 3) Use props or smaller ranges to make the sequence feel restorative. 4) A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.
